stem: A child with suspected nephritic syndrome has urinalysis sent; which proteinuria pattern is most consistent with this syndrome?

options.text: Mild to moderate proteinuria that is non-nephrotic
Proteinuria only with severe renal impairment
No proteinuria is part of the syndrome

explanation: Mild to moderate non-nephrotic proteinuria is the expected pattern in nephritic syndrome.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because proteinuria can be present in nephritic syndrome.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because nephritic syndrome typically causes mild to moderate, non-nephrotic proteinuria rather than heavy nephrotic-range loss.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because heavy nephrotic-range proteinuria is more typical of nephrotic syndrome.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because proteinuria is not limited to cases with severe renal impairment.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because proteinuria is part of the classic urinalysis pattern in nephritic syndrome.
